# Psalm 57 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Al-Tashcheth [Do-Not-Destroy]. Of-David. A-Miktam, when-he-fled from-before Saul in-the-cave.

**2** Be-gracious to-me, O-God, be-gracious to-me, for in-You my-soul takes-refuge; and-in-the-shadow of-Your-wings I-take-refuge, until destruction passes-by.

**3** I-call to-God Most-High, to-the-God who-accomplishes [all things] for-me.

**4** He-sends from-heaven and-saves-me; He-puts-to-shame the-one-who-tramples-me. Selah. God sends His-steadfast-love and-His-truth.

**5** My-soul [is] in-the-midst of-lions; I-lie-down [among] those-who-devour — the-sons of-man whose-teeth [are] spears and-arrows, and-their-tongue a-sharp sword.

**6** Be-exalted above-the-heavens, O-God; above-all the-earth [let] Your-glory [be].

**7** A-net they-prepared for-my-steps — my-soul bowed-down; they-dug before-me a-pit — they-fell into-its-midst. Selah.

**8** My-heart is-steadfast, O-God, my-heart is-steadfast; I-will-sing and-make-music.

**9** Awake, my-glory! Awake, harp and-lyre! I-will-awaken the-dawn.

**10** I-will-give-You-thanks among-the-peoples, Lord; I-will-sing-praise to-You among-the-nations.

**11** For great to-the-heavens [is] Your-steadfast-love, and-to-the-clouds Your-truth.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **57:9**: 'I will awaken the dawn' — the psalmist doesn't wait for morning; he summons it with music. Praise anticipates deliverance.

— EMET
